title.narrative: Provision of Essential Sexual and Reproductive Health and Gender-Based Violence Response Services for Populations Affected by Cyclone Chido in Cabo Delgado and Nampula.

description.narrative: Cyclone Chido has significantly impacted Mozambique, affecting over 174,000 people as of December 17, 2024. In Cabo Delgado Province, districts such as Mecufi, Chiure, and Pemba have suffered severe damage, alongside Namuno, Montepuez, Metuge, Macomia, and Muidumbe. In Nampula Province, over 46,000 individuals have been affected, with Memba and Erati among the hardest-hit districts. The cyclone has resulted in widespread destruction of homes, injuries, and fatalities, and disrupted essential services.In response, UNFPA is working with the Government and humanitarian partners to address the urgent needs of affected populations, focusing on women and girls who face heightened risks of gender-based violence (GBV) and limited access to sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services. Multi-sectoral assessments highlight critical gaps, including the lack of safety for women and girls, insufficient access to basic necessities, and disrupted GBV and SRH response infrastructure. In Cabo Delgado, six of the ten UNFPA-supported Women and Girls’ Safe Spaces (WGSS) and referral health facilities have been affected and are non-operational.This project aims to restore and support continuity of access to life-saving SRH services and GBV response interventions in the affected provinces. Activities include the provision of emergency health tents and Reproductive Health (RH) Kits to health facilities. Additionally, the project will provide dignity kits to adolescent girls and women, strengthen temporary accommodation centers to ensure privacy and safety, and enhance the operational capacity of Women and Girls’ Safe Spaces.
